claims.text: A compositionally graded refractory HEA based on W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V can effectively bond tungsten to CuCrZr.
A graded refractory HEA can provide a gradual transition in thermal expansion between W and CuCrZr.
A graded refractory HEA can provide a gradual transition in chemical properties between W and CuCrZr.
The graded transition reduces thermal stress in a W/HEA/CuCrZr joint.
The graded interlayer suppresses brittle intermetallic formation under fusion-reactor conditions.
Directly contacting W and CuCrZr have a strong mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients.
The thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr leads to poor adhesion.
Direct W-CuCrZr contact promotes brittle intermetallic formation in extreme reactor environments.
Magnetron sputtering can produce the proposed compositionally graded refractory-HEA interlayer.
Fusion-reactor materials must withstand elevated temperature, radiation, and mechanical stress.
Fusion divertor materials experience severe heat and particle fluxes.
Rapid thermal cycling is a typical operating condition relevant to the proposed W-CuCrZr joint.
A smooth transition in thermal expansion minimizes stress concentrations at the W/interlayer and interlayer/CuCrZr interfaces.
A smooth transition in chemical affinity prevents brittle intermetallic compounds during thermal cycling.
The graded HEA interlayer enhances interfacial adhesion between W and CuCrZr.
The graded HEA interlayer improves the mechanical integrity of the W-CuCrZr bonded structure.
The graded HEA interlayer improves joint durability and reliability under extreme reactor conditions.
Refractory HEAs have excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures and are considered promising for advanced nuclear applications.
Existing refractory-HEA performance trends support the proposed graded-interface mechanism.
A poorly optimized gradient, deposition defects, prolonged irradiation, or temperatures beyond the tested range may limit the interlayer's performance.
